name: SikaBond-58 Wood Floor
paste:
SIKABOND®-58 WOOD FLOOR: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor, November 2023, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sikabond_-58_woodfloor.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description. SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is a 1-component, solvent-free, wood flooring adhesive with good workability.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is designed for full surface bonding of solid and engineered wood floors and ply boards.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.6.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Low viscous wood flooring adhesive
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2023, Version 01.04) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.1).
    - ISO 17178: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear strength (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Adhesive can be sanded
    - Floors can be sanded after 12 hours
    - Elastic, footfall-sound dampening properties
    - Suitable for use with underfloor heating
    - Very low emissions
    - Reduces stress transfer between the wood floor and the substrate
    - Good bead stability
    - Good workability and plasticity
    - Low VOC content
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane
    - Colour: Parquet brown
    - Density: 1.30 kg/l approx. (ISO 1183-1)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: 35 approx. (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: 1.3 N/mm²approx. (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: 360% approx. (ISO 37)
    - Shear strength: 1.1 N/mm² approx., 1 mm adhesive thickness (ISO 17178)
    - Service temperature: +5 °C to +40 °C
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 600 ml foil pack; 16 kg metal pail
    - Shelf life: SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor has a shelf life of 12 months from the date of production, if it is stored properly in undamaged, original, sealed packaging, and if the storage conditions are met.
    - Storage conditions: SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor shall be stored in dry conditions, protected from direct sunlight and at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and homogeneous, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. Paint, cement laitance and other poorly adhering contaminants must be removed.
    - Concrete and/or cement screeds must be ground and thoroughly cleaned with an industrial vacuum.
    - Anhydrite screeds, including flowable anhydrite screeds must be ground and thoroughly cleaned with an industrial vacuum shortly before bonding with the adhesive starts.
    - Broadcast mastic asphalt must be primed with Sika® Primer MR Fast or Sika® Primer MB. For the instructions for use, please refer to the corresponding Product Data Sheet.
    - Glazed ceramic and old existing ceramic tiles must be degreased and cleaned with Sika® Aktivator-205, or the tile surfaces must be ground and then thoroughly cleaned with an industrial vacuum.
    - Wood and/or gypsum boards (e.g. chipboard, plywood) must be glued and/or screwed to the substructure in order to be fixed to the substrate. For floating dry-floors, contact our Technical Service Department.
    - For other substrates contact our Technical Service Department for advice and assistance.
    - For broadcasted mastic asphalt, cement based floors with excessive moisture content and use over old adhesive residues or on weak substrates use Sika® Primer MB. For detailed instructions contact our Technical Service Department.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: Full Surface Bonding: 800−1300 g/m² with notched trowel
    - Sag flow: SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor spreads very easily whilst maintaining stable trowel marks.
    - Curing rate: 4.5 mm/24 hours approx. (23 °C / 50% r.h.)
    - Tack free time: 60 minutes approx. (23 °C / 50 % r.h.)
4.3 Instructions.
    - For the application of SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor all standard construction guidelines apply.
    - For further information, please refer to the Method Statement "Full Surface Bonding".
4.4 Application method / tools - Full Surface Bonding with a Trowel.
    - SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is applied directly from the pail to properly prepared substrates and uniformly spread with a notched trowel.
    - SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor can also be applied from foil packs using an application gun.
    - Press the wood floor pieces firmly into the adhesive so that the wood floor underside is completely covered with the adhesive. The pieces can then be joined together using a hammer and an impact block. Many types of wood floors also have to be tapped into position from above. A distance of 10−15 mm from the wall to the wood floor must be maintained.
    The floor shall be walked on and/or sanded 24 hours after installation (23 °C / 50% r.h. up to 1 mm adhesive thickness depending on the environmental conditions and adhesive layer thickness).
    Fresh, uncured adhesive on the wood floor surface must be removed immediately with a clean cloth and if necessary also cleaned with Sika® Remover-208 or Sika®TopClean-T. Always test wood floor surfaces for compatibility with Sika® Cleaner-208 before use.
    The guidelines of the wood floor manufacturer apply.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208 and/or Sika® TopClean T. Once cured, residual material can only be removed mechanically.
4.6 Limitations and important considerations.
    - SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is only suitable for use by professional wood floor applicators.
    - For good workability, the adhesive temperature shall be ≥ +15 °C.
    - For proper curing of the adhesive, sufficient ambient humidity / moisture is necessary.
    - A preliminary adhesion test is necessary before any application on glazed tiles.
    - Before wood floors may be installed in non-insulated areas, such as basements or other areas without a damp proof membrane, Sikafloor® EpoCem must be applied and sealed with Sika® Primer MB to control the moisture. For detailed instructions, contact our Technical Service Department.
    - For use with chemically pre-treated types of wood floors (e.g. those produced or treated with ammonia, wood stain, timber preservative) and woods with a relatively high oil content, SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is only to be used with the written agreement of our Technical Service Department.
    - Do not use on polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE / Teflon), and other similar plasticized synthetic materials.
    - Some other floor priming materials can negatively influence the adhesion of SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor (pre-trials recommended).
    - SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor is designed as a wood floor bonding adhesive. When laying parquet type wood floors without tongued and grooved joints, e.g. mosaic parquet floors, avoid the wood floor adhesive extruding into the joints between the wood pieces.
    - Avoid contact between any wood surface sealer coatings and adhesive. However, if direct contact with the adhesive is unavoidable, then the compatibility must be checked and confirmed before use of any coatings. For further information and advice, please contact our Technical Service Department.
    - Do not expose uncured SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor to alcohol containing products as they may interfere with the curing reaction.
    - For further information and advice, please contact our Technical Service Department.
4.7 Further information.
    - Safety Data Sheet
    - Pre-treatment Chart Sealing and Bonding
    - Method Statement "Full Surface Bonding"

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +15 °C to +35 °C
5.3 Relative air humidity. 40% to 70%
5.4 Substrate temperature. During laying and until SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor has fully cured, the substrate and ambient temperatures shall be between +15 °C and +35 °C without and between +20 °C and +35 °C with underfloor heating.
5.5 Substrate moisture content. Permissible substrate moisture content without underfloor heating:
    - 2.5% CM for cement screeds. (ca. ~4% Tramex / Gravimetric weight percent)
    - 0.5% CM for anhydrite screeds.
    - 3–12% CM for magnetite flooring (depending on the organic content).
    - 1.8% CM for cement screeds. (ca. ~3% Tramex / Gravimetric weight percent)
    - 0.3% CM for anhydrite screeds.
    - 3–12% CM for magnetite flooring (depending on the organic content).
    Permissible substrate moisture content for use with underfloor heating:
    Note: For all moisture contents, the quality of the substrates and surfaces, always follow the guidelines of the wood flooring manufacturer.
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.6):
    - For good workability, the adhesive temperature shall be ≥ +15 °C.
    - For proper curing of the adhesive, sufficient ambient humidity / moisture is necessary.
    - Before wood floors may be installed in non-insulated areas, such as basements or other areas without a damp proof membrane, Sikafloor® EpoCem must be applied and sealed with Sika® Primer MB to control the moisture. For detailed instructions, contact our Technical Service Department.
5.7 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - A preliminary adhesion test is necessary before any application on glazed tiles.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: 1.30 kg/l approx. (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: 35 approx. (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: 1.3 N/mm²approx. (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: 360% approx. (ISO 37)
    - Shear strength: 1.1 N/mm² approx., 1 mm adhesive thickness (ISO 17178)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaBond®-58 Wood Floor, November 2023, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sikabond_-58_woodfloor.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaBond 58 Wood Floor SF, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/5/MSDS%20SikaBond-58%20Wood%20Floor%20SF%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
